title: Quality Improvement Committee Charter: Appeals and Grievances Quality of Care Cases
content:
Under **Appeals and Grievances**, a Quality of Care Grievance is handled by referral to the quality improvement committee, and no grievance alters a benefit decision.

## Charter clause

A Quality of Care Grievance is referred to the quality improvement committee, the provider has the case type's provider response period to respond, and the member is told the case was reviewed and acted on without the confidential peer review findings. A grievance never changes a benefit decision; a member who disputes a decision is told of the appeal route.

## The clause in parts

| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| Referral | Every Quality of Care Grievance goes to the quality improvement committee |
| Provider response | The provider concerned has the case type's provider response period to respond |
| What the member is told | That the case was reviewed and acted on |
| What the member is not told | The confidential peer review findings |
| Effect on benefit decisions | None: a grievance never changes a benefit decision |
| A member who disputes a decision | Is told of the appeal route |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A member raises a safety concern about a facility. The Quality of Care Grievance is referred to the quality improvement committee; at its close the member learns that the case was reviewed and acted on, but not the peer review findings.
- A member files a Member Grievance about billing and, in the same call, disputes a denied claim. The grievance does not change the claim decision; the member is told of the appeal route for the dispute over the decision.
